## Overview

IC-14 telemetry series: frozen contract, version 1.0.0 (roadmap WP-TEL-01, NEW-IC-14, spec B4).

Every Operate consumer reads site telemetry through this contract: dispatch and forecasting (B2),
the control room (B5), the ledger and baselines (B6), the twin (B7), the NESO performance files
(B3-04) and the independent verifier (B6-05). The edge gateway (B1) and the site twin produce it.
Spec §10A has no telemetry contract; the roadmap calls this one NEW-IC-14.

Spec → this contract:

=====================================  =======================================================
roadmap WP-TEL-01                      here
=====================================  =======================================================
point naming                           `PointName` (asset kind, asset id, quantity, measurement
                                       role, aspect), `point_key`, ``series_id`` =
                                       ``<org>/<site>/<point key>``
units                                  `QUANTITY_TABLE`: one canonical integer unit, sign and
                                       range per quantity; converters to IC-3/IC-5 kW, kWh and
                                       tenths of a degree with a stated rounding side
time bases                             `RESOLUTIONS` (20 Hz, 1 s, 1 min raw; 1 s, 1 min, 30 min
                                       curated), fixed UTC blocks of integer slots,
                                       `ClockStatement`, `settlement_period_of`, `age_at`
quality flags                          `ValueQuality` (on a value) and `GapReason` (on a gap),
                                       each mapped to one OPC UA status code (`QUALITY_MAP`)
raw and curated tiers                  `TelemetryBatch` (raw, immutable, hash-chained),
                                       `CuratedSeries` (a pure function of raw, recomputed by
                                       hash), `DqAnnotation` (a finding that cites raw)
tenant segregation key                 `TenantKey` on every record, `read_guard` over IC-13
=====================================  =======================================================

**A missing sample is a gap, never a zero.** A block of a series is a run-length tiling of its
slots by `ValueRun` (integers, one quality) and `GapRun` (a reason, and no value field at all).
Every slot is covered exactly once, so a sample cannot go missing silently, and a gap has no
number that could be read as zero. A curated interval is an `Aggregate` only when its usable
time reaches the method's ``min_usable_ms``; otherwise it is a `CuratedGap`. Nothing is
interpolated, held or scaled up across a gap, and a ``held`` value (OPC UA
UncertainLastUsableValue) is never usable. Fill and substitution are not in this version.

**Names and units.** A point's quantity fixes its unit, sign and range, so a unit cannot be
declared wrongly: watts, var, VA and watt-hours, mHz, mV, mA, basis points of state of charge
and thousandths of a degree Celsius, all integers. Power follows the load convention: positive
flows from the grid side into the named asset (site import, battery charging); export and
discharge are negative. Energy is two non-negative cumulative registers. A meter point and its
SCADA counterpart differ only in ``role`` (`counterparts`). Comparing with IC-3 or IC-5 converts
upward exactly (`kw_to_w`); a figure emitted in kW states its rounding side (`w_to_kw`).

**Time.** Raw resolutions are a closed table (50 ms, 1 s, 1 min); a block spans 60 s (20 Hz and
1 s) or 30 min (1 min), its ``origin`` is a whole multiple of the span on the UTC epoch, and slot
``i`` covers ``[origin + i·period, origin + (i+1)·period)``. Curated windows are one block at
1 s, 1 min or 30 min (a UTC day of 48 settlement half-hours, IC-3's grid). Intervals are
half-open and labelled by their start. The GB clock never appears on the wire;
`settlement_period_of` maps a UTC half-hour to its local settlement date and period (46, 48 or
50 a day). Each block states who stamped it and whether the clock was synchronised; a block
stamped on an unsynchronised clock keeps its values in raw, curates to ``clock_untrusted`` gaps
and reads as ``clock_untrusted`` in `age_at`.

**Tiers.** One raw batch is one block of one series, chained per (series, sender, stream epoch)
by ``prev_batch_hash`` from the IC-13 genesis value; a new stream epoch names the head of the one
before. Late delivery after a link outage (store and forward, B1-05) is normal: `track` accepts a
late fill and refuses only a fork or a changed descriptor inside an epoch. A curated record embeds
its whole `CurationMethod`, lists the raw runs it read (`RawSpan`, committed by their head
hashes) and the annotations it considered, so `verify_curated` recomputes it byte for byte. A
late batch, a changed method or a changed annotation set makes a new revision that supersedes the
old by hash (`check_supersession`).

**Tenancy.** Every record carries a `TenantKey` (the data-owning IC-13 organisation and the site)
and a ``data_class``; ``series_id`` is prefixed by the key, and the key is inside the content
hash. A data-returning reader needs a `ReadDecision` from `read_guard`, which is IC-13
`authorise` on a ``telemetry`` resource; a denied decision or a record of another tenant raises
`TenantReadRefused`, and a transform given two tenants raises `MixedTenants`.

**IC-5.** A raw batch is shaped to travel edge to cloud: ``kind`` is ``telemetry_batch``, it
carries ``site_id`` (IC-5's header rule) and it can name the IC-5 link profile and link epoch it
was sealed under (`Ic5Binding`). IC-5 1.0.0 has no telemetry body; carrying the batch inside an
IC-5 frame is an additive IC-5 minor owned by IC-5. Until then batches travel on their own
northbound channel. This module does not import IC-5 (that minor would import this one).

Version: ``CONTRACT_VERSION`` (a ``Literal`` on every record); JSON Schemas frozen at
``schemas/ic14_series_descriptor.v1.0.0.schema.json``, ``ic14_telemetry_batch``,
``ic14_curated_series`` and ``ic14_dq_annotation``; human-readable specification generated at
``specs/ic14_telemetry_series.v1.0.0.md``; git tag ``GIT_TAG``. Reads IC-13 (`IdentityClaims`,
`ResourceRef`, `ScopeGrant`, `authorise`, the audit genesis hash) and IC-4 (`EvidenceRef`, the 1.x
range).

## Schema `ic14_series_descriptor`

### `SeriesDescriptor`

IC-14 v1.0.0: one series, declared once and bound by hash into each of its batches and curated records. A changed descriptor starts a new stream epoch.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brick_class` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` or `NotApplicable` | yes |  |
| `contract` | `"IC-14"` | no | `"IC-14"` |
| `contract_version` | `"1.0.0"` | no | `"1.0.0"` |
| `data_class` | one of `"neura_operational"`, `"customer_commercial"`, `"customer_personal"` | yes |  |
| `freshness` | `FreshnessPolicy` | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"series_descriptor"` | yes |  |
| `max_batch_bytes` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |
| `meter` | `MeterBinding` or `Unknown` or `NotApplicable` | yes |  |
| `name` | `PointName` | yes |  |
| `plausible_max` | integer; >= -9007199254740991, <= 9007199254740991 | yes |  |
| `plausible_min` | integer; >= -9007199254740991, <= 9007199254740991 | yes |  |
| `record_class` | one of `"live"`, `"synthetic_fixture"` | yes |  |
| `resolution` | one of `"event_20hz"`, `"operational_1s"`, `"standard_1min"` | yes |  |
| `series_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |
| `source` | `SourceAddress` or `NotApplicable` | yes |  |
| `source_scaling` | `SourceScaling` or `NotApplicable` | yes |  |
| `tenant` | `TenantKey` | yes |  |
| `unit` | `Unit` | yes |  |

### `Aspect`

Values: `whole`, `phase_l1`, `phase_l2`, `phase_l3`, `supply`, `return`, `ambient`, `internal`

### `AssetKind`

Values: `site_boundary`, `bess`, `pcs`, `pv`, `genset`, `chiller`, `crah`, `ups`, `it_load`

### `EvidenceRef`

A reference to an IC-4 instance by its content hash (what IC-1 and others embed).

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contract` | `"IC-4"` | yes |  |
| `contract_version` | string; pattern `^1\.(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)$` | yes |  |
| `evidence_hash` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"evidence_ref"` | yes |  |

### `FreshnessPolicy`

When a series reads stale and when lost (`age_at`). Required, with no default.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"freshness_policy"` | yes |  |
| `lost_after_ms` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |
| `stale_after_ms` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |

### `MeasurementRole`

Values: `revenue_meter`, `operational_meter`, `scada`, `device_reported`, `setpoint_echo`, `derived`

### `MeterBinding`

The meter behind a metered point and its certificate (IC-4), or ``unknown`` until the meter registry (WP-TEL-04) holds it.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `certificate` | `EvidenceRef` or `Unknown` | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"meter_binding"` | yes |  |
| `meter_id` | string; length <= 120, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` | yes |  |

### `NotApplicable`

A term that does not exist for this record (e.g. a LIFO position on a firm connection). Distinct from `Unknown`: "not applicable" is a statement about the agreement, "unknown" is a statement about our knowledge of it. Both carry a reason.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"not_applicable"` | yes |  |
| `reason` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |

### `PointName`

What a series measures: one quantity, on one asset, in one measurement role and aspect. Its canonical string is `point_key`; site and tenant are not part of it (they are on the record).

### `Quantity`

Values: `active_power`, `reactive_power`, `apparent_power`, `energy_import`, `energy_export`, `frequency`, `voltage`, `current`, `state_of_energy`, `state_of_charge`, `temperature`

Where the edge reads the point (provenance, never identity).

|---|---|---|---|

Values: `modbus_tcp`, `sunspec`, `iec61850_mms`, `dnp3`, `iec60870_5_104`, `bacnet_ip`, `snmp_v3`, `opc_ua`, `mqtt`, `simulated`

### `SourceScaling`

How the adapter turns the source's number into the canonical unit: ``raw * scale_num / scale_den + offset``, rounded half to even at the adapter.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"source_scaling"` | yes |  |
| `offset` | integer | yes |  |
| `scale_den` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |
| `scale_num` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |
| `source_unit_ucum` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |

### `TenantKey`

The data owner (an IC-13 organisation) and the site. Lender and verifier organisations never own telemetry; they read it through IC-13 scopes.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"tenant_key"` | yes |  |
| `org_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |
| `org_kind` | one of `"customer"`, `"neura"` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |

### `Unit`

Values: `W`, `var`, `VA`, `Wh`, `mHz`, `mV`, `mA`, `basis_point`, `millidegree_C`

### `Unknown`

A value that exists but is not known. Always explicit, always with a reason; never ``None``. Serialised as ``{"kind": "unknown", "reason": "..."}``. ``kind`` is required (no default) so a hand-written payload that omits it is refused rather than guessed at.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"unknown"` | yes |  |
| `reason` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |

## Schema `ic14_curated_series`

### `CuratedSeries`

IC-14 v1.0.0: one block of a series at a curated resolution, computed from raw only by `curate`, and recomputable by `verify_curated`. Identified by (series, origin, resolution, method id); a later revision supersedes the earlier one by hash.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `annotations` | array of string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `contract` | `"IC-14"` | no | `"IC-14"` |
| `contract_version` | `"1.0.0"` | no | `"1.0.0"` |
| `data_class` | one of `"neura_operational"`, `"customer_commercial"`, `"customer_personal"` | yes |  |
| `descriptor_hash` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `inputs` | array of `RawSpan` | yes |  |
| `intervals` | array of `Aggregate` or `CuratedGap`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"curated_series"` | yes |  |
| `method` | `CurationMethod` | yes |  |
| `origin` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `record_class` | one of `"live"`, `"synthetic_fixture"` | yes |  |
| `resolution` | one of `"operational_1s"`, `"standard_1min"`, `"settlement_30min"` | yes |  |
| `revision` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `series_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |

| `tenant` | `TenantKey` | yes |  |

### `Aggregate`

A curated interval with a value. ``usable_ms + rejected_ms + gap_ms`` is the period.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap_ms` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"aggregate"` | yes |  |
| `quality` | `ValueQuality` | yes |  |
| `rejected_ms` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `slot` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `usable_ms` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `value` | integer; >= -9007199254740991, <= 9007199254740991 | yes |  |

### `CuratedGap`

A curated interval without a value: too little usable time. ``reason`` is the single raw reason when the whole interval was one gap, else ``insufficient_coverage``.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap_ms` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"gap"` | yes |  |
| `reason` | `GapReason` | yes |  |
| `rejected_ms` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `slot` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `usable_ms` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |

How raw becomes one curated interval, stated in full (so the record recomputes from IC-14 alone). ``method_id`` names the method across revisions; a changed method under the same id is a ``method_change``. Every number is required: no published source sets a threshold.

| field | type | required | default |

| `stream_epoch` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |

### `TenantKey`

The data owner (an IC-13 organisation) and the site. Lender and verifier organisations never own telemetry; they read it through IC-13 scopes.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"tenant_key"` | yes |  |
| `org_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |
| `org_kind` | one of `"customer"`, `"neura"` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |

### `ValueQuality`

The quality of a value. Declaration order is the worst-of order, best first.

Values: `good`, `local_override`, `inaccurate`, `out_of_range`, `subnormal`, `held`

## Schema `ic14_dq_annotation`

### `DqAnnotation`

IC-14 v1.0.0: a data-quality monitor's finding on a series over ``[start, end)``, citing the raw it read. Raw is never rewritten; a curated record counts a finding only through its method's ``applied_findings``. A withdrawal supersedes the annotation it withdraws.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `annotation_id` | string; length <= 120, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` | yes |  |
| `contract` | `"IC-14"` | no | `"IC-14"` |
| `contract_version` | `"1.0.0"` | no | `"1.0.0"` |
| `data_class` | one of `"neura_operational"`, `"customer_commercial"`, `"customer_personal"` | yes |  |
| `detector_hash` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `disposition` | one of `"asserted"`, `"withdrawn"` | yes |  |
| `end` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `evidence` | array of `RawSpan`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `finding` | `FindingKind` | yes |  |
| `issued_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"dq_annotation"` | yes |  |
| `monitor_id` | string; length <= 120, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` | yes |  |
| `monitor_version` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `record_class` | one of `"live"`, `"synthetic_fixture"` | yes |  |
| `series_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |
| `start` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `supersedes` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` or `NotApplicable` | yes |  |
| `tenant` | `TenantKey` | yes |  |

### `FindingKind`

What a data-quality monitor found (WP-TEL-03).

Values: `gap`, `flatline`, `clock_drift`, `unit_mismatch`, `meter_scada_divergence`

### `NotApplicable`

A term that does not exist for this record (e.g. a LIFO position on a firm connection). Distinct from `Unknown`: "not applicable" is a statement about the agreement, "unknown" is a statement about our knowledge of it. Both carry a reason.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"not_applicable"` | yes |  |
| `reason` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |

### `RawSpan`

A contiguous run of one raw chain, committed by its first prev hash and its head hash.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `first_prev_hash` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `first_seq` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"raw_span"` | yes |  |
| `last_batch_hash` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `last_seq` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |
| `sender_id` | string; length <= 120, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` | yes |  |
| `series_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `start` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `stream_epoch` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |

### `TenantKey`

The data owner (an IC-13 organisation) and the site. Lender and verifier organisations never own telemetry; they read it through IC-13 scopes.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"tenant_key"` | yes |  |
| `org_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |
| `org_kind` | one of `"customer"`, `"neura"` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length <= 80, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]*$` | yes |  |

## Readers

The contract's functions, each the one way to answer its question. Signatures are the module's own annotations.

### `age_at(decision: 'ReadDecision', descriptor: 'SeriesDescriptor', batches: 'Sequence[TelemetryBatch]', at: 'datetime', max_clock_skew_ms: 'int') -> 'AgeReading'`

The data age of a series at ``at``, against the descriptor's freshness policy. Age runs from the start of the newest slot holding a usable value (any quality but ``held``); at a threshold the worse state holds. A newest block stamped on an unsynchronised clock reads ``clock_untrusted``; a value dated after ``at`` by more than the clock skew reads ``future_dated``.

### `batch_end(batch: 'TelemetryBatch | CuratedSeries') -> 'datetime'`

The end of a block: ``origin`` plus its span (half-open).

### `check_batch(descriptor: 'SeriesDescriptor', batch: 'TelemetryBatch') -> 'None'`

Refuse (`BatchRefused`) a batch that is not bound to ``descriptor`` by hash, differs from it in tenant, series, class or resolution, or holds a ``good`` value outside the plausible bounds (the producer flags such a value ``out_of_range``).

### `check_batch_size(raw: 'bytes', descriptor: 'SeriesDescriptor') -> 'bool'`

True when a received batch's bytes are within the descriptor's ``max_batch_bytes``.

### `check_supersession(old: 'CuratedSeries', new: 'CuratedSeries') -> 'None'`

Refuse (`ValueError`) a revision that does not follow ``old``: another key, a revision other than the next, another superseded hash, or a reason the change does not bear out (``late_raw`` reads strictly more raw under the same method and annotations; ``method_change`` changes the method; ``annotation_change`` changes the annotation set).

### `clock_drift_ms(prev: 'TelemetryBatch', batch: 'TelemetryBatch') -> 'int'`

Wall-clock advance minus monotonic advance between two blocks of one edge boot, in ms (signed). WP-TEL-03 compares it with the IC-5 profile's ``max_clock_skew_ms``.

### `counterparts(name: 'PointName', names: 'Iterable[PointName]') -> 'tuple[PointName, ...]'`

The points of ``names`` that measure the same thing as ``name`` in another role (a revenue meter and its SCADA reading, say), in role order.

### `curate(descriptor: 'SeriesDescriptor', batches: 'Sequence[TelemetryBatch]', annotations: 'Sequence[DqAnnotation]', method: 'CurationMethod', origin: 'datetime', resolution: 'CuratedResolution', prior: 'CuratedSeries | NotApplicable') -> 'CuratedSeries'`

The curated record of the block at ``origin``, from the raw batches inside it and the annotations considered. With a ``prior`` revision, the result supersedes it, for the reason that differs: the method, else the annotation set, else the raw read (``late_raw``).

### `current_revision(records: 'Sequence[CuratedSeries]') -> 'CuratedSeries'`

The newest revision of one curated block; refuses a fork (two records superseding one hash), a second first revision, or records of another key.

### `effective_annotations(annotations: 'Iterable[DqAnnotation]') -> 'tuple[DqAnnotation, ...]'`

The asserted annotations that no other annotation of the set supersedes, sorted by hash.

### `from_opcua(code: 'int') -> 'ValueQuality | GapReason'`

The member mapped to an OPC UA status code. An unlisted code raises: an adapter maps it explicitly or emits a ``configuration_error`` gap; there is no fallback by severity.

### `kw_to_w(kw: 'int') -> 'int'`

IC-3/IC-5 kW in W, exactly.

### `kwh_to_wh(kwh: 'int') -> 'int'`

IC-3/IC-5 kWh in Wh, exactly.

### `millideg_to_tenths_c(value: 'int', side: 'Side') -> 'int'`

Thousandths of a degree as whole tenths, rounded to the stated side.

### `parse_point_key(key: 'str') -> 'PointName'`

The `PointName` whose `point_key` is ``key``; raises `ValueError` on anything else.

### `point_key(name: 'PointName') -> 'str'`

The canonical string of a point: ``asset_kind.asset_id.quantity.role.aspect``.

### `read_guard(claims: 'IdentityClaims', tenant: 'TenantKey') -> 'ReadDecision'`

IC-13 `authorise` for a read of ``tenant``'s telemetry by validated ``claims``. Never raises on denial: a denied read is audited too.

### `require_certified(descriptor: 'SeriesDescriptor') -> 'EvidenceRef'`

The meter certificate behind a series; raises `NotCertified` unless it is an IC-4 reference (the registry resolves it and holds class and accuracy).

### `resample(batches: 'Sequence[TelemetryBatch]', annotations: 'Sequence[DqAnnotation]', method: 'CurationMethod', origin: 'datetime', resolution: 'CuratedResolution') -> 'tuple[Aggregate | CuratedGap, ...]'`

The curated intervals of the block at ``origin``: pure, raw input only. A raw slot no batch covers is ``not_recorded``; a slot of a block stamped on an unsynchronised clock is ``clock_untrusted``; a value of an unusable quality, or under an applied annotation, is rejected. An interval holds a value only with ``min_usable_ms`` of usable time.

### `resource_ref(tenant: 'TenantKey') -> 'ResourceRef'`

The IC-13 resource a read of this tenant's telemetry targets (and an audit event names).

### `settlement_period_of(start: 'datetime') -> 'tuple[date, int]'`

The GB settlement date and period (1 to 46, 48 or 50) of the UTC half-hour starting at ``start``. UTC to local only: the period is counted from local midnight.

### `slot_instant(batch: 'TelemetryBatch | CuratedSeries', slot: 'int') -> 'datetime'`

The start of slot ``slot`` of a block.

### `split_import_export_w(value_w: 'int') -> 'tuple[int, int]'`

A signed active power (load convention) as IC-5's two non-negative terms, (import, export) in W: at most one is non-zero and import minus export is the input.

### `tenths_c_to_millideg(tenths: 'int') -> 'int'`

IC-3/IC-11 tenths of a degree in thousandths, exactly.

### `to_opcua(member: 'ValueQuality | GapReason') -> 'int'`

The OPC UA status code of a quality or gap reason.

### `track(state: 'TrackState', batch: 'TelemetryBatch') -> 'tuple[TrackState, TrackVerdict]'`

The receiver's verdict on an arriving batch, and the state after it. Late delivery is normal (store and forward); only a fork, or a changed descriptor inside an epoch, is refused, and a refused batch leaves the state unchanged.

### `values_in(decision: 'ReadDecision', batches: 'Sequence[TelemetryBatch]') -> 'tuple[SlotValue | SlotGap, ...]'`

The slots of ``batches`` in time order: each value with its quality and whether its clock was trusted, and each gap as one interval with its reason. Raises `TenantReadRefused` unless the decision allows a read of every batch's tenant.

### `verify_batch_chain(batches: 'Sequence[TelemetryBatch]', *, prior_epoch_head: 'str | None' = None) -> 'str'`

Check a complete, in-order run of one chain (series, sender, stream epoch) and return its head hash. A run starting after seq 0 needs no genesis; ``prior_epoch_head``, when given, must be the head the epoch names.

### `verify_curated(record: 'CuratedSeries', descriptor: 'SeriesDescriptor', batches: 'Sequence[TelemetryBatch]', annotations: 'Sequence[DqAnnotation]') -> 'None'`

Recompute ``record`` from raw and refuse (`ValueError`) any difference: the descriptor, the raw runs it names (each span's chain links and end hashes), the annotation set, and the record's own content hash.

### `w_to_kw(value_w: 'int', side: 'Side') -> 'int'`

W as whole kW, rounded to the stated side (ceil against a cap, floor against a floor).

### `wh_to_kwh(value_wh: 'int', side: 'Side') -> 'int'`

Wh as whole kWh, rounded to the stated side.
